#4128. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

#4127. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4126. How To Identify Stolen Items In Probably Stolen

What counts as stolen goods, who brings them in, and how to get away with selling them in Probably Stolen.

You know, for a game labeled Probably Stolen, it's pretty easy to play an entire run without dealing in stolen property at all. But that's no fun; who doesn't want to play the bad guy sometimes? Or at least, the morally grey guy.

If you're interested in dealing with some not-so-legally-acquired goods to make a profit, here's what you need to know and who you need to avoid.

Typically, stolen goods will be things like pharmaceuticals, chemistry products, or sometimes food. All stolen goods will have some level of heat attached to them based on their value in credits. Heat is the game's metric for how obviously stolen they are — higher heat objects will be easily identified as stolen by buyers and Security, while low heat items might be easier to get away with. Heat disapates over time; the longer you have the item in your inventory, the less attention it'll attract. When it hits zero heat, it's no longer considered stolen and can be sold normally.

Stolen goods are also typically sold by a shady customer or, in some cases, wanted criminals. They'll say something to the effect of needing to get rid of their goods quickly, of "finding" them, or similar phrasing. Sometimes the customer will simply be labeled Thief, which does make identifying them much easier, but sometimes you'll be buying from a chemist or pharmacist who's stolen from their workplace.

On day 14 (or day five if you skip the intro), you'll be visited by The Butcher, a wanted Lower Levels criminal who sells meat that's identified as stolen with fairly high heat...don't ask where the meat comes from. He comes back once a week to sell off his goods. You can choose to report him to Security if you want to, but that can have some pretty dire consequences. You can also try shooting him with the shotgun, but this isn't particularly effective. This is, in my opinion, one of the scariest characters in the game.

How to inspect goods, evaluate their worth, and level up your appraisal skills in Probably Stolen.

Storing stolen goods is relatively easy; keep them in a smuggler's bay, which can hold up to a five by five grid of objects. This isn't a ton of room, but you can get an expanded smuggler's bay using the Underground Exchange (you'll need to leave a normal smuggler's bay and eight Oxymore injectors in your trash can overnight), which holds an eight by eight grid of objects.

Put stolen goods into your smuggler's bay immediately upon buying them; don't call up your next customer until they're put away if you can avoid it. My first run of Probably Stolen ended because I got caught with stolen goods on the counter one too many times by Security and got arrested.

Once they're in the smuggler's bay, you can sell off your stolen goods to anyone willing to buy them. Don't try and sell them to Security, for obvious reasons, but most Lower Levels citizens won't care where their product came from as long as you have what they need. ou can hold onto stolen goods until their heat is gone if you want to sell them off normally; again, once they hit a heat of zero, they can safely be removed from the smuggler's bay.

Be careful selling stolen goods; every sale of a good with heat attached to it ups your Possession (Stolen Goods) crime, which can eventually lead to an arrest, which ends your run. To combat this, you can hire Joe Wild's Fixers through his network, who will, for a nightly fee, eliminate these crimes from your record, which can keep you from getting arrested.

Which upgrades should you invest in at the beginning of your next Probably Stolen run for more money or better perks later on?

#4125. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

#4124. Shigeru Miyamoto To Receive The Inaugural 'Legend Award' At The 30th D.I.C.E. Awards

Award will be presented only once per decade

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has announced that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, said the following:

“Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards."

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the company would even exist today without his creations.

He most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a new demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

#4123. Nioh 3 is killing it on Steam with over double the series' highest concurrent player count

People seemingly haven't been able to stop playing Nioh 3 since the moment it came out, and everyone helped push the numbers to unprecedented heights for the series.

Nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

Nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

#4122. Love and Deepspace ushers in the Year of the Horse with a Wuxia-inspired AU multi-banner and a restaurant management mini-game

A new Love and Deepspace banner event is here with a lot of rewards to earn, and brand-new Memories for all five lads to unlock.

Love and Deepspace has kicked off the next big in-game moment and is celebrating Chinese New Year with the arrival of a new 5-Star Memory Series. This year's spring-themed banner is available now until February 27, and it comes with a host of events.

The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

The new memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

Some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the new Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the new event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a new mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

Furthermore, if you log in for 10 days throughout the event, you can unlock a new outfit set, Wealth Overflow, which can be worn by any of the love interests as well as the heroine. There are other login rewards, too, like 10 Deepspace Wishes, 10 Empyrean Wishes, His and My Outfit sets, two dynamic portrait photo poses, and loads more.

Finally, the Golden Fortune event adds even more daily log in rewards in the form of one free "shake" per day, from which you can earn a random reward of between 68 and 108 Diamonds — that adds up to a total of 1,296 Diamonds if you show up every day.

#4121. Black Mesa’s Latest Update is the Next Best Thing to Half-Life 3

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight. You’d think that 22 years after the release of Half-Life 2, it would hurt any less, but nope.

In a bid to soothe aching hearts and Gordon Freeman enthusiasts all around the world, the wizards over at Crowbar Collective have put out a new update to Black Mesa, making the 2020 love letter to Half-Life look better than ever.

This update, branded a ‘red letter day’ by the developers, focuses first and foremost on visual improvements. Crowbar Collective has managed to make the game look better, while also significantly improving its performance in the process.

After around 20 years at Treyarch, Call of Duty Zombies writer Craig Houston has been laid off, prompting tributes from fans and former colleagues.

In a showcase by the developers, scenes previously clocking around 130 FPS now reach 170 FPS. It’s not clear how these improvements will scale on different hardware, but expect to see noticeable changes across the board.

On the eyecandy side of things, interiors have now been updated to use parallax-corrected cubemaps (PCC). This technique turns static reflections into dynamic ones by adjusting them based on the player’s perspective. As a result, it adds a lot of depth to interiors while not incurring costs on the performance side. Translucent materials like glass have also been updated to have light behave realistically as it passes through.

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight.

While interiors got plenty of jazz, there have also been major improvements to the game’s environmental lighting as a whole. Crowbar Collective has improved the Source Engine’s light bouncing, making indirect illumination behave more realistically. Outdoor scenes have received image-based lighting, using HDR to bring more accurate outputs.

As a love letter to Valve’s magnum opus, it’s only natural for Black Mesa to cater to the company’s handheld console. Following the update’s performance improvements, Black Mesa has received the Steam Deck Verified badge.

The latest update to Black Mesa has modernized the user interface to make it behave better with stick controls, benefiting both Steam Deck and PC users who play with controllers. According to Crowbar Collective, keyboard and mouse have also been refined. Nostalgics can still pick the classic Half-Life menu from the Steam Workshop.

The popular Blue Shift mod by HECU Collective, which tells the game’s story through the eyes of Barney Calhoun, has been updated to be compatible with the latest version of Black Mesa.

For now, this massive update to Black Mesa is all we have until the yearly ritual of hoping for a Half-Life 3 reveal at The Game Awards. Earlier this year, Valve composer Mike Morasky alluded to a certain game codenamed ‘HLX’, which some of the more hopeful types have taken to be a working title for the much anticipated sequel.

That is not the first time Morasky has run his mouth about the HLX project, so maybe, just maybe, this time it’s for real. Until more evidence surfaces, you’ll find me playing Black Mesa.

Black Mesa is available via Windows and Linux platforms via Steam.

#4120. PlayStation Sends Out Update Warning Ahead Of GTA 6 Launch

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

We're now on the cusp of what will likely be the biggest gaming event in our lifetimes: the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Anticipation for the title has been high for years, and increased marketing over the last few months has driven hype to unprecedented levels. Millions have pre-ordered, and pre-installation has been available for a week, allowing players to have the game on their consoles ready for the moment it goes live.

For those of you who downloaded GTA 6 on your PlayStation 5 and then left the console alone, Sony has a warning: there's a hardware update you'll need to complete between now and midnight to make sure you're ready for launch.

I pre-installed my copy of Grand Theft Auto 6 yesterday, but before I did that, I was hit with a new PlayStation 5 hardware update. I couldn't complete my GTA preload until it was done.

Preloads were made available before the hardware update dropped, though, and there are likely plenty of people out there who downloaded the game and turned their PS5s off until it launched. These people will be hit with the hardware update when they go to play Rockstar's title, delaying their entry into Vice City.

PlayStation issued a warning to these people. It reads:

Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.

The message was so important that Rockstar retweeted it, as did the PlayStation regional accounts.

The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of those occasions where unity may be achieved. There will be millions of excited players starting their journeys tomorrow, sharing stories with friends and those on social media. It's already the most preordered game of all time, and it sits atop every single PlayStation Store chart, so it's going to be huge. It even managed to scoop seven Game Awards nominations, and it hasn't even been released yet.

#4119. Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores.

That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day."

There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

#4117. Grand Theft Auto 6 Review: a Once in a Generation Open-World Achievement

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

If there’s one thing Rockstar can never be accused of, it’s rushing out Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been so long since the (still incredible) GTA V launched that there are people who weren’t born at the time who are now teenagers (no, you’re not old enough to play yet, son, and go to bed!).

It’s not like Rockstar wasn’t busy during that time — they’ve been constantly updating the ever-growing Grand Theft Auto Online and also happened to release one of the greatest westerns of all time in Red Dead Redemption II. Yet all of the many years of development somehow becomes immediately apparent the second you pass the title screen. Put simply, this is one of the largest and most ambitious games ever created.

GTA 6 centers around the complicated personal and professional relationship of two criminals, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and their journey through the realistically hard-to-succeed-in world of Vice City. That’s about the only story element I’m comfortable sharing, however, as this is a game that begs not to be spoiled and to be experienced as fresh as possible.

GTA VI’s main story is full of crazy twists and turns, surprising emotional beats, and yes, absolutely hilarious moments that push boundaries and envelopes. Along the way, you’ll meet a cast of colorful characters that will quickly endear themselves to you and ones you’d commit many virtual felonies to defeat out of seething hatred.

While the campaign is gripping and exciting all the way through, there are so many stories just waiting to be discovered in GTA VI. It feels like a living, breathing world which is all the more impressive considering there are basically no loading times or slow down upon entering a loaded save.

There’s a ton of traffic through the roads (so much so that you can’t just easily blaze through like a bowling ball as easily as in previous games), the drivers get actively mad if you crash into them, and there are NPCs going about their days on every corner. You could make a whole game into simply approaching NPCs and seeing what they’re up to — there are some surprisingly interesting happenings going on and it’s rare that even the most minor of characters repeats themselves.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

While you can follow the main story all the way through, complete tons of side quests or simply take part in what the most depraved of us do and make the game into a rampage simulator, there are so many activities here that almost any one of them could be focused on as a full game. There’s diving for treasure, bird watching, fishing, customizing cars and oh so many other things that are fully fleshed out and not just throwaway afterthoughts.

In fact, just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim. Upon awakening, you can eat, make coffee, watch TV, play video games, workout, watch a show, do home repairs, feed pets and enough other tasks to make a list of them as long as a full review.

It’s incredibly cool for the world to feel so realistic that you literally sometimes get stressed out from knowing you have to do a chore and can’t just go run people down (I guess I am one of the depraved ones after all). Sometimes an hour is spent in GTA VI literally lifting weights, drinking a protein drink, grocery shopping and laying down in bed doomscrolling. While that might not exactly be the sentence to sell you on the game, the fact that GTA VI is just that deep and manages to make it all enjoyable to carry out truly speaks to the attention to detail at play.

The realism also carries over into the gameplay mechanics themselves. Driving feels more realistic than it ever has. It’s easy to get wanted stars and hard to shake the cops, and people will get actively pissed off at you for doing the wrong thing. In fact, it’s realistic to the point that some might not have as much fun as they did in previous titles as you will think twice before hijacking a random car or even parking it in the wrong place (yes, the fuzz can be called on you for leaving your car at an NPC’s house).

Just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim.

It goes beyond simply just blazing through the world doing horrible things and hoping a cop doesn’t see it — there are immediate and severe consequences to your actions now.

That being said, it’s hard to criticize Rockstar for the game being too realistic, and once you adapt to its ebb and flow, this new realistic GTA experience feels all the more enveloping as it stimulates the anxiety, stress and fear synapses as much as the happiness ones, making successful accomplishments in the game all the more rewarding.

It’s impossible to review GTA VI without touching on the music, and if I had my way, this entire review would just be speaking about that. But as I don’t want to risk you clicking out since we could really use those GTA page views, I’ll keep it short.

The score itself is composed by famed French electronic duo, Justice, and is like an aural hug to the ears. The instrumentals during key action scenes are some of the best heard since HEALTH’s stunning Max Payne 3 score and get the adrenaline pumping.

The included original songs Justice recorded are so expertly crafted to sound like ‘80s hits that I was literally googling the lyrics thinking I had found long lost ‘80s songs before realizing it was actually Justice. Considering I’m big Justice fan who’ve seen their live show multiple times, that says a lot that they even fooled me.

Rockstar has released GTA 6’s launch trailer, spotlighting Jason and Lucia while confirming Justice as the composers of its original score.

It’d be fair to judge a GTA by its radio stations as they play such an integral part in the experience and are heard for literally hundreds of hours by most players, so thankfully there’s another incredible lineup here. There’s a channel for everybody — ranging from buttrock to country to reggae to classical music to many, many more.

Fans of past channels like Radio Broker and Radio Mirror Park will be happy to hear that there’s another hipster/indie style channel in GTA VI dubbed “Stockyard FM” which plays music from the likes of Hot Chip, Nation of Language, !!! and even debuts a new song from the aforementioned HEALTH. Flash FM quickly becomes a favorite as well, focusing on high energy dance pop and electro pop from artists like Billie Eilish, The Ting Tings and more.

Finally, Circoloco Records is a commendable addition featuring smooth throwback-style electronic music from Rockstar’s own record label. But expect to hear a fantastically curated soundtrack no matter which station you jam out to, with artists ranging anywhere from The Weeknd to Steve Winwood.

With how many flawlessly-executed mechanics and elements to GTA 6 there is, it’s hard to find faults. There’s not even many glitches that occur, which is shocking for an open world game of the magnitude.

Possibly the only criticism would be that it's so complex and ambitious that the learning curve is steep, and even after dozens of hours in the game, it’s easy to forget how a certain mechanic works or which button does what at times. Of course, criticizing something for being so deep proves difficult and at the very least perhaps a good problem to have in the end.

Rockstar has minimized the complexity as much as they could by providing an easy-to-access control list at all times and basically devoting the first twenty or so hours of the story as a backdoor tutorial.

Considering how enormous the scope of GTA 6 is, it’d be easy to forgive it for having visuals not up to snuff, yet it boasts some of the most realistic character models seen in gaming and uses them throughout all of the beautifully-choreographed in-game cutscenes.

The way the characters are rendered give them a certain unique realistic element that has never quite been captured before — from unique body types to random skin marks to life behind the eyes. As good as the characters look, the environments might look even better with everything from trees to the pavement itself rich in detail. There’s also incredible lighting work at play that makes everything pop like you’d expect Florida, er, Vice City to.

While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time. And one of the best driving games of all time. And one of the best…birding…games of all time? It may sound like hyperbole, but GTA VI is so chock full of content that it feels like several fully-fleshed out games in one. And that’s not to mention it actually does have several fully-fleshed out games within a game inside of it. GTA VI may not completely reinvent the wheel, but it fully commands it, delivering an enormous adventure that’s chock-full of enough things to keep you busy until Grand Theft Auto VII (please, Rockstar?). The last thirteen years were more than worth the wait and make Grand Theft Auto VI go down as an unparalleled achievement in video games.

#4115. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4114. GTA 6 Custom PS5 Pro Gifted To Miami Heat Players

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

In recent years, there have been some stunning (and not-so-stunning) limited-edition custom consoles. These are often created to promote a game and are usually available in limited quantities via competitions and giveaways. In 2019, Xbox commissioned 12 custom Xbox One consoles to celebrate the launch of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, and more recently, it shoved a Series X down an alligator's throat.

This new one is a real head-turner, though, and it's one that you'll almost certainly never see in person, as Rockstar just gifted players of Miami Heat custom Grand Theft Auto 6 PlayStation 5 Pro consoles.

Grand Theft Auto's Vice City is heavily based on Miami. Grand Theft Auto 6 takes that a step further, with Leonida looking very much like Rockstar's version of Florida. The parallels are so great, in fact, that Rockstar turned the city of Miami into Vice City.

It's painted electrical boxes, taken over the airport, and a nightclub has temporarily changed its name to match the one in GTA 6. It's also opened up Burger Shot shops for people to get GTA's burgers in real life, and perhaps most notably, will take over the Miami Heat basketball team for one night. It's set to wear limited-edition jerseys, and the court has been redecorated with the infamous blue and pink of Vice City.

The collaboration seemingly didn't stop there, either. Over the last few hours, Miami Heat players, including Myron Gardner, Davion Mitchell, and Tim Hardaway Jr., have posted stunning PS5 Pro care packages they've received from Rockstar.

Delivered in a custom suitcase, the players received two limited-edition Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 DualSense controllers, a copy of Grand Theft Auto 6, and a custom PS5 Pro console. The console is a slick silver color, etched with palm trees and the VI from the GTA logo. The vent running across the middle is metallic pink and blue.

These are some of the coolest consoles we've ever seen, and for what will likely be the biggest media event for many, many years. It's just a shame that we'll probably never get to lay our eyes on them in person.

#4113. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4112. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

#4111. GTA 6 Ties for the Best Reviewed Game of All Time

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

Rockstar has finally proven the doubters wrong, as Grand Theft Auto VI is officially tied for the best-reviewed video game of all time, with only Nintendo’s greatest retro title managing to keep up.

Expectations for Grand Theft Auto VI were sky-high going in, especially after being delayed on multiple occasions, with Take-Two and Rockstar promising that the game needed more polish and would be worth it in the end. There were some doubters, but the fact that Take-Two was leaving money on the table meant that most fans had faith it would live up to expectations.

The embargo for Grand Theft Auto VI went up as soon as the game went live on New Zealand’s Microsoft Store, and the scores are in. It seems that Rockstar is ending 2026 with a bang, as Grand Theft Auto VI has obliterated the competition, at least in terms of reviewer opinion.

Denkiworks explains why Tanuki: Pon's Summer launched between Zelda and GTA 6, and why the small studio believes the risk was worth taking.

The Metacritic page for Grand Theft Auto VI is live, and the results are in. Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

One outlet that gave Grand Theft Auto VI a 10/10 is DualShockers, with Steve Hennley writing, “While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time.”

Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

The only game to match Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64, which also has a 99. Funnily enough, the game’s remake came out this year, and it scores slightly lower than Grand Theft Auto VI, capping out at a 96 on Metacritic.

That being said, a trip to Hyrule might be the only option for a lot of people, as Grand Theft Auto VI is currently a PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S exclusive. This means that Nintendo Switch 2 and PC owners will have to find out games to play. Maybe it’s time to break out Garfield Kart and pretend he’s running over civilians?

It was always likely that Grand Theft Auto VI would score well, considering Rockstar’s amazing library of titles and the sheer amount of time and money that went into its latest game. The delays might have been frustrating, but if the result was the best-reviewed game of all time, then it was worth it.

With the help of XBOX Cloud Gaming, even last generation's XBOX console will be getting in on the fun.

The question now is what the fans will think, as only people in New Zealand can currently play the game. Oh, and the people on Xbox Series X/S who have suddenly traveled to Middle-earth and switched their region to New Zealand (don’t worry, no one will tell John Microsoft). After all, it’s not unheard of for the critical and audience reviews to differ greatly.

The verdict from the fans will filter in over the next few days and weeks, but until then, Rockstar and Take-Two can lean back and know they have a stacked accolades trailer ahead of them, and that Vice City will have millions of visitors over the upcoming holiday season. If the reviewers are correct, a once-in-a-generation game has arrived, and it’s time to dive in.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4110. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4108. GTA 6 Review - An Astounding, Impossible New Bar For Video Games

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

Throughout much of my nearly 100 hours of playtime, reviewing Grand Theft Auto 6 felt like a paradox. Finally getting a chance to see what Rockstar has been cooking for close to a decade is both the most exciting moment of my whole career and the most high-pressure thing I’ve ever been lucky enough to take on. How do you possibly begin to talk about something that had whole studios built just for its NPCs?

GTA 6 is the biggest video game of all time, but we really only knew the basics. Something that dawned on me less than an hour in when it became clear just how much had been held back. Even with the weight of 13 years of anticipation on my shoulders, I’m also well aware that nothing I say about Jason and Lucia’s felonious tour of Leonida will influence the minds of anyone even half interested in it.

The great irony of this herculean task is that, more often than not, Grand Theft Auto 6 left me completely speechless, pointing at the screen and gibbering like an idiot at what Rockstar has accomplished. By every measure, it’s a masterclass of a game that not only lives up to the impossible hype but somehow goes even further by redefining what it means to be a GTA game.

Following the narrative heights of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its beloved Arthur Morgan is an unenviable task, but Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn’t disappoint. It follows Jason and Lucia, two small-time criminals who reunite and are quickly forced to rise through the ranks of Leonida’s underworld after a failed job puts them up against Vice City’s most dangerous forces.

So far, so GTA, but there’s more to the plot than the rags-to-riches setup would have you believe. Unsurprisingly, I can’t tell you much about the overarching story and what sets it in motion, but Jason and Lucia’s involvement has far more emotional and mature stakes than any other game in the series before it. Rockstar takes the pair to places I never would have predicted (including some surprisingly dark moments), and it all lands because of how expertly written and characterised both protagonists are.

Jason is more stoic and guarded than any of the more out-there characters we followed throughout Los Santos, but he’s got a heart of gold and lots of charm underneath the gruff exterior, which mostly comes out when he’s with Lucia. He’s harder to read and takes time to warm up to, but by the end, Jason stands comfortably alongside the series' most memorable protagonists, Niko, CJ, and even Red Dead’s revered gunslingers.

Lucia, on the other hand, is without a doubt the best protagonist in Grand Theft Auto history. She’s fiercely loyal, emotionally mature, witty, and doesn’t take crap from anyone, almost to a fault, as her passion and eagerness to prove herself often land her in trouble. As the series’ first female lead (no, I don’t count the pixel blobs from the first game), there’s a lot of pressure on Lucia, but she easily reaches the lofty bar set by Arthur Morgan.

“We believed in this idea of putting a relationship at the center of the game and trying to make a GTA that was still as funny, crazy, shocking, and fun as the previous games but with added heart. But yeah, the process of making something like this you always question things. As you saw with the 2022 hack, game development isn’t pretty. It can take a long time and a lot of iteration to make good on an idea and to get things working. But I think simply the idea that the relationship would be something that the player needed to work at an earn (or ignore if they want to!) felt like exciting new territory.” - Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative

Of course, as great as Jason and Lucia are on their own merits, they come as a pair in GTA 6 and are together for nearly all of the story’s biggest moments. I had some doubts about the Bonnie and Clyde-style romance, as it's not exactly familiar territory for Rockstar. But after seeing their chemistry and working to give them an unbreakable bond through hand-holding, dates, clubbing, and, of course, doing crime as a pair in my playthrough, I simply can’t imagine the two not being madly in love. Some of my favourite moments in the whole game were simply taking Jason and Lucia on a date, grinning as they flirted, and getting unhealthily invested in their relationship.

It’s not just a win for the story, either, as Jason and Lucia’s cooperative gameplay is a huge step up from GTA 5, with far more options than just swapping, from letting your partner drive you to waypoints and having them cover you in firefights to asking them to fence your stolen goods or hang back as a getaway driver. In GTA 6, having a partner in crime finally means exactly that.

That romance might be the focal point and main standout of GTA 6’s story, but there’s plenty to love about the excellent supporting cast as well. Whether you’re supposed to love them like the cool-as-ice mentor figure Raul or hate them like some characters I won’t dare mention, there’s not a single weak link. Though the writing can occasionally be slightly less biting than previous games, Jason and Lucia’s tale tops GTA 4 as the series’ best narrative.

Perhaps my favourite character of the whole game is Karim, the hacker in Raul’s group who provides some surprising Watch Dogs 2 vibes.

Sony is right - Grand Theft Auto 6 is probably going to play best on PlayStation.

It would have been easy (or at least easier) for Rockstar to take GTA 5’s lucrative formula and just polish the graphics a bit, but one of the biggest strengths of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how it completely rebuilds the main tenets of the whole series. For starters, core mechanics like movement, shooting, and driving all feel far better than ever thanks to extensive improvements and tweaks.

Take GTA’s infamous mash X to sprint controls, for instance, which have been completely reworked for a more standardised and smoother experience. Jason and Lucia are both far more agile than previous protagonists and have more vertical options at every moment, which makes the simple act of getting around on foot much more enjoyable. The only downside to the rework, and spoilers for the rest of this review - the game as a whole - is that the controls can sometimes be a little overcomplicated due to how many interactions you have at your disposal.

It did take me a good few hours to adjust to the new control scheme, but it’ll be incredibly tough to go back now. There is an option for the classic version if you really struggle, though.

“There was lot a lot of internal team feedback to look at our controls and responsiveness after we launched RDR2, so we doubled down on exploring an ‘experimental’ control scheme as it was called internally at the time. The experiment kind of stalled mid development due to other competing priorities but was revitalized by Rob (Head of Development). After that, we all strongly felt it should be the default control scheme as we’d had consistently good feedback from the team and user research. We still offer classic GTA controls in the setting menu for those prefer them. Indeed, we have many people at R* who still do! There are also a lot more options for players to explore in the menu. Hopefully, there is a scheme or set of options for everyone to enjoy the game!” - David Hynd, Vice President of Technology

Shooting, meanwhile, takes cues from Red Dead Redemption 2 and its weightier weapons, which already felt inspired by Max Payne 3’s stellar gunfights. There’s even a Dead Eye/Bullet Time slow-motion focus mode for both protagonists, rather than being locked as a special ability for one character, and it becomes an essential tool as you go up against the gangs and cops of Leonida. It’s the best combat has ever felt in a Grand Theft Auto game by a country mile.

The same goes for driving, which sits somewhere between GTA 5 and GTA 4 thanks to a greater focus on vehicle weight, physics, and damage while somehow still retaining the buttery smooth controls and flow. Driving is also the most immediately obvious example of Rockstar not just improving how Grand Theft Auto 6 plays, but recontextualising every mechanic’s implementation with a greater focus on worldbuilding and player involvement.

Unlike previous games in the series where you could grab a fast car and bomb it down the city streets without so much as tapping the brakes, Leonida’s denser traffic and narrower streets (including a ton of painfully realistic roadworks) mean you need to be paying attention at all times. It’s only when you start to master the new systems and put the effort in that you can weave through traffic like a pro, which makes it infinitely more rewarding. Couple that with cars requiring far more work to attain thanks to higher security and a ridiculous amount of upgrade and modding options, and vehicles become so much more than just something you steal, park in your garage, and don’t give a second thought to.

On the other hand, gunfights are no longer about just aiming for the head with whatever arsenal you’ve got in your back pocket, as you now need to incapacitate enemies with clean, targeted shots to the knees and arms if you want to keep a professional criminal profile. You also have a more limited choice of weapons, forcing you to plan ahead and keep your trunk stocked before a firefight. Even crime, the main thing Grand Theft Auto is known for, is completely different in GTA 6. Not only are the police more advanced than ever before, with multiple stages of realistic awareness of your actions that incentivise masks, stealth, and being as efficient as possible, but there’s far more effort that needs to be put in for even the simplest of sins.

"A lot of work, yeah! There were a few key areas we needed to change for cops in particular on this game. The perception/recognition system needed a complete overhaul. On V/RDR the cops always knew where the player was located, but with the new model they now rely on proper search/investigation routines, guided by witness reports and evidence (e.g. dead bodies, abandoned vehicles). K9 units can sense the player too, so you need to keep on your toes when they are around! And, of course, we added appearance and outfit recognition to add depth/roleplay mechanics to cop evasion. Having an unknown wanted state created lots of great gameplay moments, where you could nonchalantly leave a crime scene undetected. And adding in Heat added a level of persistence that was lacking in previous games. The wanted UI also took a lot of time to finesse/balance. We added threat indicators to give the player more feedback around how they were being perceived by cops/enemies in game. This opened up some cool stealth gameplay opportunities, but was also crucial seeing as we removed enemies from the radar. Once you are spotted, we now rely on cops calling it in before you fully known. This gives the player a window of opportunity to deal with the situation before things kick off.  But yeah, it’s been a massive effort. Fueled by constant tweaks and iteration over many years." - David Hynd, Vice President of Technology

Gone are the days of completing a few story missions and having millions in the bank without anything to spend it on, as money is incredibly hard to come by in Vice City. You really need to work for it, whether through simple but low-reward gas station stick-ups and jewel store heists, or storming gang hideouts for drugs you can sell on to fences. What’s most impressive about all of the crime opportunities is that they’re completely emergent and up to the player, a massive leap forward from Los Santos story-specific heists and very basic convenience store shakedowns.

As if being able to pull off story mission-esque heists at any moment wasn’t enough, GTA 6 has also made some notable improvements to the main campaign. When they’re not trying to make Jason and Lucia feel like real people with quieter moments, story missions are energetic, bombastic, and, unlike some criticisms of Red Dead Redemption 2, give the player more freedom and control than before. While I’m sure some players will prefer the classic, more thoughtless approach, for my money Grand Theft Auto 6 is a better and more considered game on every single front, pushing the series formula to impossible new heights.

In a game that’s all triumphs, the biggest of all is Grand Theft Auto 6’s meticulously crafted world, which is so unbelievably impressive it single-handedly justifies the long wait. From the murky swamps near Leonida Keys to the neon-lit upper echelons of Capri, Leonida is jaw-dropping at every turn (fittingly for Vice City, especially at night) and a downright feat of engineering to get it all working without any issues on PS5 Pro. Some things, especially the weather system and frankly ridiculous lighting, need to be seen to be believed.

I’ve never stopped to smell the roses so much in a game, but it’s impossible not to soak in all of the work and love that’s gone into every explorable interior, every beach packed with NPCs you can interact with or just hear have detailed conversations, every neighbourhood with potential things to steal, and every flea market with functioning shops. Almost all of the effort feels necessary to deliver on the promise of Leonida, but you can often feel Rockstar flexing its penchant for the little details (such as food being realistically eaten and the unique games that are playable on the PlayStation parody) that make these worlds feel so real.

Grand Theft Auto 6 also easily has the best radio selection the series has seen since Vice City. Justice’s original soundtrack is also incredible and punctuates major story moments perfectly.

Rockstar’s foray into heightened realism in Red Dead Redemption 2 has clearly left its mark on GTA 6, which focuses heavily on immersion and realism. You can shower, work out at the gym to build muscle, eat food to put on weight, get tired from not sleeping enough, need to keep vehicles filled with fuel, and have more hairstyle and clothing options than you know what to do with. I was a little worried it’d go too far and end up a little intense like RDR2, but Rockstar has taken the right amount of inspiration from that game while still making sure GTA isn’t getting too close to a life-sim.

“I personally love going into a gas station, buying a hot dog and a slushie and walking out alternating between eating and drinking and walking down the street doing that, then throwing the empty cup in the trash. I love getting a six pack of beers and walking along drinking them one at a time, throwing them around!”- Rob Nelson, Head of Development

Beyond being so detailed and immersive, Leonida is also just an incredibly varied and handcrafted county that feels unique no matter where you go. It’s a far cry from GTA 5’s handful of city areas mixed with vast wilderness that ends up getting ignored, and it helps that it’s stuffed with side missions, minigames, and emergent events that keep the water-cooler spirit Rockstar’s games are so well known for.

It might feel like I’ve said a lot about GTA 6 (it certainly does to me, anyway), but even with close to 100 hours, there are still whole areas I’ve barely explored, mechanics I’ve only glanced at, easter eggs to find, and activities that are begging for more of my time - it’s an absolute juggernaut. There’s also so much I can’t talk about or simply don’t want to get into to keep the sense of discovery for everyone else.

Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best open-world game I’ve ever played, and one of the best games full stop, with only incredibly minute nitpicks barely worth mentioning that do nothing to drag it down from masterpiece status. Its jaw-droppingly detailed world, completely revamped and recontextualised mechanics, and heartfelt narrative with two stellar leads put it far above the rest of the incredible series and set an impossible new bar for the medium as a whole. I'm sure we’ll never see another game with such unreal hype that actually lives up to and exceeds expectations, but you can rest easy knowing that the long road to Leonida was worth walking.

We finally got a chance to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and it's still one of the best games ever made.

#4107. Rumour: Atlus May Be Gearing Up For A Huge Persona 6 Reveal

After what felt like an age waiting for the Persona franchise to make its Switch debut, Sega and Atlus are now all-in on the Switch 2. Persona 4 Revival is scheduled to launch on 20th May 2027, while Persona 6 has also been confirmed for the hybrid console.

Atlus is in full marketing mode for Persona 4 Revival, but our pals over at Push Square have reason to believe that the company may be gearing up to properly reveal Persona 6 in the coming weeks.

This comes from Reddit user ronakwya, who notes that Atlus recently updated the official website for Persona 6. Apparently, however, this was the kind of update that allows Atlus to perform significant changes to the website in preparation for a big public reveal.

Ronakwya has also pointed to the gameplay reveal of Persona 4 Revival as a potential hint. Its own website was also updated in a similar manner roughly one month prior to its big reveal at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026.

So, which big gaming event is taking place in just less than a month from now..? Yep, The Game Awards 2026.

This all seems incredibly convenient though, and to be honest we're a little sceptical. As pointed out by Push Square, it would make little sense for Atlus to pull attention away from Persona 4 Revival at this stage to host a full reveal for Persona 6.

In our opinion, we could definitely see a similar reveal during the Xbox Games Showcase in 2027 after the release of Revival in May (February for other platforms). We're happy to be wrong, as we're proper itching to see some gameplay from the next mainline entry, but we're not holding our breath.
