#4106. 8 Best Anime Where Friendship is Built Through Small, Everyday Moments

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

Oh, the sweet art of life known as friendship; it’s beautiful. It makes us realize just how deep human connections are forged, and that this extends to fictional media, whether it be your favorite bromances in gaming or just some of the best presentations of this bond showcased in movies, shows, or even anime.And you see, that’s exactly where some of my expertise lies, both professionally and personally. Being the only child of my parents, the only kind of sibling-like relationship I’ve had growing up, and even now, are my countless friends I’ve met online or IRL. Call it a “My friends are my Power” situation.

This list goes into extensive detail on the best romance anime where falling in love is just the beginning, but these shows prove that happily ever after is never that simple.

So, thinking about them and then my rather intermediate experience with anime, I woke up today and figured, let’s discuss some of my hand-picked anime where friendship is built through small, everyday moments. Where, no matter the ongoing circumstances that may ensue, the main cast manages to grow an everlasting bond with each other until the end of the show’s runtime.

I bet only some hardcore Kyoto Animation fans have seen this show, but trust me, it’s such a warm ray of sunshine. The series follows Tamako, a cheerful schoolgirl who spends most of her time helping at her family's mochi shop. Between school and her responsibilities at the shop, she shares plenty of moments with her best friends, Midori and Kanna.

But that balance is exactly what creates this sweet blend of friendship with the everyday life of a neighbourhood shop, pretty much exactly what you want from a slice-of-life anime. Oh, and if you want a romantic subplot payoff for Tamako, be sure to check out the sequel movie, Tamako Love Story, which is just as heartwarming as the OG show.

I’m switching tracks to a recent anime, one whose manga I read a bit of before the anime came into production. Skip and Loafer is mainly centered on Mitsumi Iwakura, a country girl who moves to Tokyo to attend a prestigious high school. While she's academically gifted, navigating the social dynamics of a city school proves more challenging than her studies. Fortunately, she meets Shima and gradually gets to know the other wildcard cast of classmates.

And while there is a romantic slow-burn development between Mitsumi and Shima, it’s not the main focus, since the main draw is Mitsumi slowly forming friendships with everyone through awkward conversations, shared school experiences, or small acts of consideration. It is genuinely a great slice-of-life seasonal show to watch from recent years of anime.

If you loved Frieren: Beyond Journey's End, this list goes into detail on the best anime to watch if you loved its delicate yet naturally paced vibe.

This one’s familiar to many readers, I hope. While Barakamon initially seems like it’s centered on a struggling calligrapher trying to reignite his creative spark, the story’s real soul comes from the surprising connections he builds after relocating to the Goto Islands.

Seishuu Handa starts out as a gifted but pretty snobbish artist who gets banished to a sleepy countryside village after an embarrassing incident, and he's so used to his quiet city life that he’s totally not ready for the lively locals who pop by his house for all sorts of reasons.

But you see, that’s the beauty of this show. Handa’s companionship with these locals slowly changes his outlook on life, especially through his interactions with the mischievous little girl named Naru. He develops a family-like bond here, and that's one reason this show is a perfect pick here.

This one’s actually one of my best friends’ favorite shows that he’s been begging me to watch for years, and I can honestly understand why. It's not only because of my fondness for Yuru Camp, but also because Non Non Biyori is one of THE defining Iyashikei (healing) shows on the block. It takes place in the sleepy countryside village of Asahigaoka, where a tiny school has only five students across different grade levels.

The anime lets you find plenty of warmth in these girls’ everyday interactions, whether it's Renge's amusing childlike observations or Natsumi and Komari's sibling antics. There is no kind of elaborate storyline either; it’s simply one of the coziest shows in the medium.

If you wanted peak relatability, then look no further than Hitoribocchi no Marumaru Seikatsu. That name is a mouthful for anyone preferring English titles, I know, but bear with me if it's your first time hearing about this cute little show because it’s fit for anyone who’s ever tried to get out of their comfort zone.

It’s about a girl named Hitori Bocchi (no, not the pink-haired anxiety rockstar) who is so anxious that talking to classmates feels like a final exam, but her goal of making friends is so adorable yet a little painful to watch. What I love is the show’s patience because her victories are tiny, like a successful greeting or a shared lunch, and the show treats each moment as a milestone.

With how many are airing, there are some Anime Series You’re Probably Missing Out on in 2026.

As much as I wanted it at the top for personal reasons, it’s also fine to include Yuru Camp here, because I could gush about it endlessly.

The series follows Rin Shima, a girl who enjoys camping alone, and Nadeshiko Kagamihara, an outgoing newcomer who shares her enthusiasm for exploring the outdoors, even if her initial impression here is sleeping on a bus stop bench at night. Their initial encounter eventually brings them into contact with a wider circle of friends at their school who also enjoy spending their free time camping as well.

The show is one of the best modern healing anime out there, especially since it teaches you so much about camping itself with Rin and the others’ trips. Even better is how it takes place at actual campsites and in key locations across Japan’s rural prefectures and towns.

It would’ve felt wrong not to mention K-On! on this list, especially given the whole emphasis on anime friendships with this list. What starts as an attempt to save her school's Light Music Club eventually becomes one of anime's most endearing friendships, as Yui Hirasawa joins Ritsu, Mio, and Tsumugi despite having practically no musical experience.

Of course, the girls spend plenty of time practising, but that's hardly what makes their relationship so enjoyable, since their afternoons are just as likely to involve drinking tea, chatting about random, inconsequential things, or finding excuses to avoid doing any actual work. Even after Azusa joins the club, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another is a genuine delight.

To me, if there’s one anime that defines a goofy, whimsical yet endearing friendship, it's Azumanga Daioh. Originally released in 2002, this beloved slice-of-life comedy follows six high school girls with wildly different personalities: the exceptionally gifted Chiyo Mihama, the absent-minded Osaka, the energetic Tomo, the short-tempered Yomi, the quiet, reserved Sakaki, and the competitive, eccentric Kagura.

Much of the show revolves around everyday moments, whether it's studying together, going on summer vacations, or simply finding new ways to annoy one another with all kinds of tomfoolery; these girls will always find a way to make you grin at the slightest bit of their lighthearted banter or actions.

And you see, watching this group become increasingly comfortable with one another throughout their high school journey makes their inevitable graduation feel incredibly bittersweet. It’s genuinely one of the shows my friends and I have come to adore, not because of its niche memes, but because there’s an actual heartwarming friendship here that grows with each episode.

#4105. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4104. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

#4103. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4101. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Crowned 2026's "Best-Selling Physical Video Game In The US"

The Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 got off to an outstanding start, selling over five million copies (approx 5.2 million units) in just four days. Sales in the UK and Japan have contributed to this, and now, Circana Retail Tracking Service has shared data about the title's US launch.

As highlighted by Circana's senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella (via social media), "after just one week", Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is this year's "best-selling physical video game in the US". Interestingly, it's the first title to surpass one million physical units in a US launch week since the 2023 Switch title, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Considering the year is almost over, and Grand Theft Auto 6's retail release is actually a "code-in-box", we imagine Ocarina's remake will hold onto the title of 2026's best-selling physical game (that's actually a proper physical game). However, there is one technicality - Circana tracks and reports "code-in-box" sales as "new physical video game sales", so Zelda may not actually keep the crown. And GTA 6 has already smashed pre-order records.

According to Nintendo's official data, Ocarina of Time is currently the second-highest selling Switch 2 game globally. As we previously noted, this puts it ahead of Donkey Kong Bananza's lifetime sales of 5.05 million, and the Switch 2 launch title Mario Kart World leads with 16.48 million sales. So it's still a tremendous effort for the remake of the legendary N64 title.

In our review here on Nintendo Life, we awarded Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake 9/10 stars, calling it the "best way to play one of the most seminal games of all time". After a brief dip to 95, it's once again sitting on a Metacritic score of 96/100.

#4100. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score.

Did you pick up The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week? Let us know what you think of it so far in the comments below!

#4099. Nioh 3 is, unsurprisingly, the fastest-selling game in the series with over a million units sold

Nioh 3 has taken the Nioh franchise to new heights, delivering its biggest-ever launch.

Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Today, publisher Koei Tecmo has announced that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”

If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

#4098. GTA 6: The Big Review Round-Up

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

With less than 24 hours until Grand Theft Auto 6 launches, the game's review embargo has lifted, and it's everything we expected it would be. The game opened to a staggering 99 on both Metacritic and OpenCritic, making it officially the best-reviewed game of all time. If there were any doubts that Rockstar might fumble the bag, they have now been put to bed.

Its glowing reviews are best captured in quotes from critics around the world. We've trawled through these reviews and gathered them into a full round-up featuring the thoughts from some of the industry's most notable reviewers. Hopefully this will amp up your excitement another notch ahead of tonight's release.

We'll start off with our very own George Foster, who delivered an astounding 5/5 review. He called it the most "high-pressure thing" he's ever taken on, but it seems like it was worth it. The game constantly left him "speechless," and he says it sets "an impossible new bar for the medium," but his thoughts are perhaps best summarized in the comment below:

"Without a shadow of a doubt, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the best open-world game I’ve ever played, and one of the best games, full stop, with only incredibly minute nitpicks barely worth mentioning that do nothing to drag it down from masterpiece status."

Unsurprisingly, GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain also scored the game a 10/10. He said, "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7."

Josh West had the honor of reviewing GTA 6 for GamesRadar+. They were seemingly just as blown away by the game as everybody else, saying, "With impossible production values, details that matter, and an interconnected set of world systems that bring this world to life, GTA VI is unlike anything we’ve ever seen. Jason and Lucia are the beating heart of this game, and the story they tell is worth living. This isn’t just a good game, or a great game, it’s the kind that comes just once a generation."

The 10s keep rolling in, with Luke Reilly giving it another perfect score for IGN. They said, "I was simply not ready for just how much richer, deeper, and more satisfying Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be. After three weeks and over 120 hours playing it, I’m still hopelessly hooked, absorbing the world at walking speed like a tourist in a new town. I’m dazed by just how consistently I find myself noticing a new animation, unique pedestrian, or standout vehicle. I am completely enamoured with its series-best car handling and weaving through the realistically dense traffic. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

VGC's Jordan Middler said the game "does so much at such a high bar" in their 5/5 review. Like many of his fellow reviewers, Middler felt that it's a game that will likely never be matched. "This is Rockstar operating at the absolute peak of its power. The scale of Grand Theft Auto 6’s achievement won’t be felt this week, or next week, or even next year. It’ll be felt in the next decade of games that come after it, as developers, like so many before them, attempt to emulate the Rockstar magic. But nobody else can. No one has the budget, this number of developers, and this level of cultural impact."

One of the few 9/10 scores came from The New York Times and Yussef Cole. While not quite a 10, they were still enamored with the game, saying, "The surprising depth to which themes are explored makes for a memorable and endearing experience in Grand Theft Auto VI, which largely lives up to its sky-high expectations by inverting the series’s reputation for destruction."

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4097. Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

#4096. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4095. Halo: Campaign Evolved Gets Firefight Mode In Free Update This Winter

Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free update this winter, an Xbox Wire post announces. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.

Firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry.

Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.

#4094. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4093. Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Has Been Updated To Version 1.1.4

Konami has released a new update for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse on the Switch and other platforms this week.

Although it's only a small one, it does include some adjustments and fixes. This includes a slight change to the "effective range" of the "Life Drain" spell. Here's the rundown from Konami's official website about everything included in the Version 1.1.4 update:

The following changes and fixes have been made in this update: - The version number is now displayed at the bottom of the title screen. - Adjusted the effective range of the “Life Drain” spell. - Fixed an issue where the screen could remain black after loading under certain conditions. - Fixed various other issues.

Belmont's Curse is currently available for the Switch. While there's no Switch 2 Edition, if you do play this title on Nintendo's new hardware, you'll get a frame rate boost. And if you haven't tried it out yet, you can download a demo from the eShop.

You can find out more about this new Castlevania entry iun our review here on Nintendo Life. We gave it 8/10 stars, calling it "one of the best Castlevania games in a long time thanks to its combat variety and smart whip integrations".

#4092. YouTubers Share Their Amazing Home Videos From The Most Important Day In Xbox History

Happy birthday, Xbox! It's exactly 25 years today since the original Xbox console launched in North America on November 15th of 2001, and it turns out multiple people captured the moment via some amazing home video footage.

We've talked about one of these videos before — the ridiculously cool one from MyRetroLife, who has become a YouTube star since uploading his footage multiple years ago. His short clip of "booting up an original Xbox on launch day" has a whopping 4.6 million views, while his more elaborate story about it (which you can watch down below) has almost 900,000 views.

We're not affiliated with him, but you should go check out his other stuff as well - it's really entertaining!

It turns out there's more footage on YouTube from November 15th that we weren't aware of though, with this next example coming from The Great Gambino. They have much less of a high-profile following than MyRetroLife, but their three-minute Xbox footage is equally as interesting and nostalgic to watch, so it's well worth a view!

Apparently, this video was somewhat quietly uploaded to their YouTube channel a few years ago, but exploded into the millions of views after other people reposted it to the likes of TikTok, Facebook and other social media platforms.

They uploaded the most complete version of it a couple of years ago, which you can see below:

Of course, some of us Pure Xbox users were also there back on November 15th of 2001, unboxing our original Xbox consoles for the first time, but it's quite special to see the moment captured on camera for us to see in 2026!

#4091. GTA 6 Already Has 2.5 Million Twitch Viewers

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

The last 30 minutes have been, quite frankly, massive for the world of video games. Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews dropped, and it's officially the highest-rated game ever released. The review embargo coincided with the game's release in New Zealand, as midnight struck in that territory. Players are now starting to get their hands on the game.

While some are opting to take "sneaky flights," changing the time on their consoles to gain access to it early, others have just opted to passively view things. Within 30 minutes, the game has broken the Twitch record for the most-viewed single-player game of all time, and it's undoubtedly about to break the most-viewed game record imminently.

Before today, according to Guinness World Records, the most-viewed single-player game of all time on Twitch peaked at 1,280,000. That was Hogwarts Legacy, back in 2023. 30 minutes after launch, Grand Theft Auto 6 obliterated that record.

As of right now, there are over 2.5 million viewers in the GTA 6 category on Twitch, each one itching to get an early view of what the game contains. Streamer Alanzoka has 227,000 viewers alone, and others like xQc and TheBurntPeanut have 99,000 and 48,000, respectively.

The multiplayer record looks set to tumble shortly. According to TwitchTracker, League of Legends holds the record for the most concurrent viewers for a multiplayer game, peaking at 3,111,023 back in November 2022. Grand Theft Auto 6 is 80 percent of the way there, and half of the United States, Twitch's biggest audience, is still asleep. Valorant holds the record for most viewing hours in a single day at 34 million, but there's almost no chance it'll hold on, with GTA likely to smash it today.

Prior to release, the game was already breaking records, becoming the most preordered game in history, with at least 10 million preorders. That was nine days before release, so that almost certainly doubled. If you're planning to play at midnight in your local time, just make sure you follow PlayStation's latest piece of mandatory advice.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4090. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4089. Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production

Wolfenstein 3 is officially underway at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced.

The announcement of the third mainline Wolfenstein title in MachineGames’ trilogy comes over seven years after the launch of the fourth and most recent spin-off entry, Wolfenstein: Youngblood. Sharma’s announcement includes a teaser image of the script for Wolfenstein 3's first chapter. MachineGames echoed this reveal with its own post, which includes a photo of a motion capture session featuring actress Debra Wilson, who plays Grace Walker in the series.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh

MachineGames’ last release was 2024’s well-received Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, but studio co-founder Jerk Gustafsson stated in a NoClip documentary last year that he hoped to finish BJ Blazkowicz’s story. Based on Gustafsson’s comment, it sounds like Wolfenstein 3 very recently started production, so we probably shouldn’t expect any substantial update for a good while.

This won’t be the only new Wolfenstein project, as Amazon is developing a live-action series based on the franchise. Until either the new game or the show releases, you can tide yourself over by reading our reviews of Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, and Wolfenstein: Youngblood.

#4088. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4087. God Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next Monday

It's been about nine months since Sony Santa Monica and Mega Cat Studios dropped God of War Sons of Sparta as a surprise reveal and launch during a State of Play. If you haven't checked it out yet, the developers are giving you some new reasons to today, unveiling two new modes and a new platform: PlayStation 4.

If you don't remember, God of War Sons of Sparta is a prequel spin-off of the God of War series, showing protagonist Kratos as a 13-year-old soldier, long before his god-killing days. The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.

Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.

For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

#4086. PSA: Splatoon Raiders Demo Splashes Onto The Switch 2 eShop Today

Splatoon Raiders made quite the splash when it arrived on the Switch 2 earlier this year, and if you haven't already had a chance to try it out, there's now a demo.

You can download this demo from the eShop, and it comes loaded with three stages set in the Spirhalite Islands, three preselected loadouts, and reunites you with the crew from Deep Cut.

Of course, this title is somewhat different to the mainline experience. It's more of a story-driven experience, where you work your way through stages and waves of enemies to progress to the next stage and unlock more weapons, upgrades and content. It also offers co-op multiplayer, if you do want to team up with family and friends.

According to Nintendo's latest financial sales data, Splatoon Raiders has now sold 2.42 million copies, placing it in the top-ten best-selling games on the Switch 2. We awarded it an "excellent" 9/10 stars when it arrived in July, noting how it offers one of the most enjoyable gameplay loops on Nintendo's new system.

In some related news today, Splatoon 3 has been updated to Version 12.0.0. It includes changes to multiplayer and much more. You can find out more in our previous story. The last game update for Splatoon Raiders was in August.

#4085. Talking Point: As Xbox Celebrates Its 25th Anniversary, What Are Your Hopes For The Next 25 Years?

Maybe we'll be looking back on this in 2051!

The celebrations for Xbox's official 25th anniversary roll on! We've finally arrived at November 15th, which marks the exact date when the original Xbox launched all the way back in 2001. How time flies!

Of course, this is a great chance to reflect on everything that's happened over the past 25 years, which we've been doing in various articles throughout the month (and indeed the year), but it's also an opportunity to think about the next 25 years and where Xbox as a brand might be headed in the future.

I think the cynical view, and perhaps the logical view, is that Xbox won't exist by the time we get to 2051. Let's not forget that PlayStation was still in its infancy 25 years ago, SEGA had just got out of the console business after being a major player for so long, and Nintendo hadn't even released the GameCube in North America until November 18th of 2001.

Feature 25 Years Later, How Many Of These Original Xbox Launch Titles Have You Played?

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

In other words, 25 years is a very long time, and we've seen many ups and downs from Xbox throughout its history. The glory days of Halo, Xbox Live and the Xbox 360 were followed up by a horribly botched Xbox One launch, and the Xbox Series era has been summed up as everything from extremely promising to extremely disappointing, now hovering somewhere in the 'cautiously optimistic' territory for some Xbox fans since Asha Sharma took the helm earlier in 2026.

While console sales might be down, and the Xbox CEO keeps talking about a need to "return to growth", there's every reason to believe Xbox might still be a powerhouse in 25 years' time. Microsoft's backing is obviously a big aspect of that — assuming the brand never gets sold off — but so is the mountain of incredible first-party IP (Minecraft, Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, etc.) that should continue to rake in money over the next decade at least, coupled with the ability to innovate in the hardware space and eventually win back some market share with handhelds and consoles.

Realistically, the answer to all of this is that we don't have an answer - it's impossible to predict a future that's still 25 years out, especially when Xbox's mission statement appears to have changed on an almost yearly basis during the 2020s. There's no doubt that Xbox will face many challenges in the 25 years that are ahead and it'll be forced to adapt and innovate along the way, but I wouldn't be surprised if we're still talking about it in 2051!

For what it's worth, here's what Xbox boss Asha Sharma said on this topic a few days ago:

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this. [..] A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

#4084. How Wuthering Waves Brings Its Evolving World to Life Through Character Design, Music and Storytelling

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, Kuro Games.

Solaris-3 is a world still recovering from the Lament, a cataclysm that reshaped its land and left Tacet Discords roaming the ruins. Players enter it as the Rover, a wanderer with no memory, and rebuild their understanding of the world one region at a time.

Since launch, that world has grown far beyond its starting point in Huanglong. Rinascita, Lahai-Roi and now the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou in Version 3.7 have each added new cultures, new Resonators and new mysteries to uncover. Version 3.8 sets the stage for the next major chapter, paving the way for Version 4.0 and the arrival of the New Federation.

But Wuthering Waves does more than add new places and faces. It gives every addition meaning through three connected creative pillars: character design, music and storytelling. Together, they turn new content into something players feel, not just something they unlock.

In Wuthering Waves, a Resonator's outfit is a passport. Costume, color, silhouette and animation tell you where a character comes from and what role they play, often before they say a word.

The clearest example is Rinascita, whose cast looks like it belongs to a single, coherent culture while each member stays distinct:

If the costume introduces a character, animation brings them to life. Jinhsi, the Magistrate of Jinzhou, moves with poised, ceremonial grace that suits a leader. The Shorekeeper's calm, drifting motions reflect her role as a quiet guardian of the Black Shores. Even an Intro Skill becomes a small character beat.

Each new region gives Kuro Games a new artistic direction to explore, from Huanglong's flowing robes to Rinascita's carnival and gladiator styles, and on to the tribal and futuristic looks of Lahai-Roi. The cast grows more varied with every update, yet still reads as one world.

If character design tells you who belongs where, music tells you how it feels to be there. The soundtrack's strength comes down to three ideas: genre fusion, musical world building and lyrics that tell stories.

Wuthering Waves rarely sticks to a single genre. A track might set its mood with synthesizers and programmed drums, then hand the melody to strings, piano or electric guitar. Cartethyia's "With Glory I Shall Fall" blends orchestral instruments with synth bass and electric guitar: the orchestra brings grandeur, while the guitar and bass add urgency and a modern edge. The mix is deliberate, matching a world where ancient tradition and advanced technology sit side by side.

The soundtrack changes its musical vocabulary as you travel. The music of Huanglong is anchored by sweeping melodies and traditional instrumental timbres, creating a tranquil yet deeply narrative atmosphere. Rinascita’s soundtrack is brighter and more vibrant, blending romanticism with dramatic tension—echoing the seaport city-state’s rich artistic heritage. Meanwhile, Lahai-Roi leans toward a modern pop aesthetic, complementing its science-fiction, academic setting. You can sense a region's identity through its music before you know its history.

Vocal tracks are part of the storytelling, not decoration. Phrolova's theme, "Reveries in the Crimson Beyond", speaks to a dream as if asking it for comfort and company, reflecting her longing to stay inside an imagined world and hold on to moments she has lost. Players who know her story hear the lyrics differently, and the song in turn deepens their understanding of her.

The emotional power of Wuthering Waves’ music does not end when players leave the game. Through To the New World, the game’s first global concert tour, its music travelled from the virtual world into reality, visiting six cities—Shanghai, Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and Los Angeles—and attracting nearly 50,000 attendees worldwide. Blending orchestral performances, live vocals, band arrangements and immersive stage productions, the concert brought familiar melodies and character themes to life in new ways. It also rekindled memories of pivotal story moments and beloved characters, giving players the chance to relive those emotions together and experience a second emotional resonance with the game.

That commitment has also earned industry recognition. After “Against the Tide” won the 2025 HMMA for Song – Video Game (Console & PC), Wuthering Waves received three more nominations in 2026—across original song, mobile-game music and live concert performance. These honors reflect how the game treats music not merely as accompaniment, but as the emotional heartbeat of its characters and world.

The world of Wuthering Waves feels alive because its story never stops moving. Characters change, conflicts shift, and places carry the marks of what happened there.

The Rover's search for lost memories is the thread that runs through every region. Each Main Quest chapter pulls the Rover deeper into the mysteries of the Lament and the forces shaping Solaris-3, giving players a reason to keep moving forward.

The larger plot matters because the people in it do. Character-related quests explore what drives each Resonator: their loyalties, their losses and the choices they struggle with. When a Resonator you know steps into a Main Quest, the stakes feel personal.

Each region introduces its own culture, politics and conflicts. Huanglong wrestles with duty and protection, Rinascita with faith and tradition, and Lahai-Roi with knowledge and the future. Version 3.7 brought the Xuanfang arc to its finale in the Simulacrum Nexus of Mengzhou.

Not every story is told in dialogue. Ruined cities, overgrown battlefields and quiet landmarks hint at the history behind them, rewarding players who explore and look closely.

Every major update adds a new chapter of history, a new set of characters and a new storyline. Instead of a fixed world, Solaris-3 is one that keeps changing alongside the people who live in it.

Wuthering Waves is at its best when design, music and story work as one, and nearly every Resonator in the cast is built this way. Here are three examples of how it works.

Design. Cartethyia’s dual-form design brings her past and present together. Her Cartethyia form reflects the free wandering knight she has become, while Fleurdelys recalls the Blessed Maiden, vessel of Divinity and Queen of Gale and Tide she once was. Fate bestowed upon her the title of the Blessed Maiden, but it was her own choices that gave the title its true meaning.

Music. Her theme, "With Glory I Shall Fall", mirrors that duality. Orchestral grandeur speaks to the legend of the Blessed Maiden, while electric guitar and synth bass bring the force of the warrior who fights for Rinascita.

Story. Her story gives both of them meaning. Once you learn how the title of Blessed Maiden came to rest on her shoulders, her two forms and her theme stop being separate details and become one character.

None of the three would land as hard alone. Together, they make Cartethyia unforgettable.

Design. One of Aemeath's most distinctive design features is the transformation between her human and mech forms. The mech is a transformation form born from her past as an Exostrider Synchronist, as well as an extension of her own abilities. Elements of Fleet Snowfluff's design are also incorporated into the mech, making it both a reflection of her childhood admiration for heroes and an essential means through which she fights and protects others. The seamless transitions between her two forms, along with their cooperative combat, further reinforce the connection between them.

Music. As the digital songstress known as Fleet Snowfluff, music plays an integral role in Aemeath's characterization. In her character teaser, Memories of Fleet Snowfluff, we see her wholeheartedly practicing her songs. Her voice fits perfectly with Lahai-Roi's contemporary pop-inspired musical style. More notably, the development team uses forward and reversed versions of the same melody to represent different timelines, connecting Aemeath's childhood and adult selves through a shared musical motif. As the truth behind her story gradually unfolds, players come to realize that these melodies had been quietly foreshadowing the emotional revelations all along.

Story. If her design and music bring Aemeath's character to life, then the Version 3.1 Main Quest reveals the reasons behind these creative choices. She was once an Exostrider Synchronist at Startorch Academy, and an ordinary girl with dreams of her own. However, after resonating with the Exostrider and pushing herself into Overclock, she lost her physical body and became a digital ghost. Her encounters with Rover also form a causal loop centered on connection, memory, and protection.

Design. Hsin is the Sentinel of Mengzhou and the first playable Sentinel. In combat she splits into fox forms, a striking image for a guardian who is more than she first appears.

Music. Her theme, "Ode to Hsin and Moon", is a vocal song composed by Jin Dazhou and sung by Jaime Arin. It comes in two versions, "Endless Yearning" and "Whither Away?", and the titles alone give her two moods: a longing that never fades, and a question of where her path will lead.

Story. Version 3.7 closes the Xuanfang arc around her. Her storyline completes the logical loop of her audiovisual design: it unveils why her character design highlights power while her music reflects an inner uncertainty, bringing both sides into unity through her story.

Three regions, three very different Resonators, yet in each one design, music and story point the same way. That harmony is what makes the world of Wuthering Waves feel alive.

Wuthering Waves keeps growing, but size is not what makes Solaris-3 memorable. What sets it apart is how each new region and Resonator arrives fully realized: dressed in a look that belongs to their culture, carried by music that gives them an emotional voice, and woven into a story that connects them to everything around them.

Through Version 3.7, that approach has taken players from the halls of Jinzhou to the carnival streets of Rinascita, the frontiers of Lahai-Roi and the heart of Xuanfang. With Version 3.8 now live, Rovers will find their paths crossing more and more with the New Federation. A new story is about to set off from here. Wherever the Rover heads next, one thing seems certain: the next chapter of Solaris-3 will be worth seeing, hearing and feeling.

#4083. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4082. Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns Of The Patriots: Part 8 – A Nostalgic Island Getaway | Super Replay

In 2008, Kojima Productions released what was billed as the swan song for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear series: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. The game had the staggering task of tying up decades of storytelling by bringing together Solid Snake, Ocelot, Otacon, Raiden, and many more characters for one explosive finale. The adventure centers on a rapidly aging Solid Snake racing against the clock to stop his twin and nemesis, Liquid Snake, one last time. Of course, there are far more bizarre shenanigans at play.

Guns of the Patriots was acclaimed for its storytelling, cinematic presentation, and evolution of the series' stealth gameplay, namely the OctoCamo suit that allowed Snake to mimic the appearance/texture of any surface he touched. It also has the distinct honor of earning a rare 10/10 review score from Game Informer. Now, thanks to the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, we can finally revisit MGS 4 without dusting off a PlayStation 3.

Join recent Metal Gear convert Charles Harte, who will be on the sticks to experience Guns of the Patriots (via the Master Collection Vol. 2) for the very first time, alongside long-time series fan Marcus Stewart, who is revisiting MGS 4 for the first time in over a decade. The stream kicks off today live on Twitch and YouTube at 12 p.m. PT/3 p.m. ET, and will continue for two hours each week until we roll credits.

If you can't catch us live, you can watch each episode after they air by following the YouTube links below.

Every week, Game Informer editors enter the vault and dust off games from every genre and platform imaginable. Watch Replay to relive fond (and not so fond) memories from gaming’s past.

#4081. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.
